citation: Yang 2025, High-precision and ultraspeed monitoring of melt-pool morphology in L-DED using deep learning, Additive Manufacturing Frontiers
task: melt-pool monitoring (melt-pool segmentation and width extraction)
sensing_modality_or_input: coaxial CCD melt-pool camera (42 fps) with pulsed auxiliary illumination
data_size: 4600 melt-pool images (augmented by translation and vertical flips)
independent_units: 20 process-parameter runs (R1-R20) on one L-DED system; 4 single tracks for width validation
model_method: lightweight U-Net (5 levels, 8-128 filters) with weighted binary cross-entropy using manually annotated weight maps; compared with FCN and R2Unet
split_protocol: "this dataset was proportionally segmented into training, validation, and test sets, wherein both the training and validation sets constituted 40 % of the data, whereas the test set constituted 20 %"; split method (random or grouped by run) not stated

citation: Scime 2023, A data-driven framework for direct local tensile property prediction of laser powder bed fusion parts, Materials
task: property prediction (local yield strength, UTS, uniform and total elongation), with powder-bed anomaly segmentation as an upstream step
sensing_modality_or_input: layer-wise visible-light powder bed images (OEM camera, post-melt and post-spreading); machine log-file sensors (layer time, gas flows, oxygen, temperatures); laser scan path data (OEM QM Meltpool position records at about 40 kHz); CAD geometry
data_size: 6299 SS-J3 tensile specimens corresponding to 29,680 super-voxel feature vectors of 21 engineered features; 230 GB co-registered dataset; segmentation network trained on about 180 million annotated pixels from 38 layers of 23 builds
independent_units: 5 builds (B1.1 to B1.5 with 503, 2705, 813, 694 and 1584 specimens) on one Concept Laser M2 printer with one powder lot; specimens extracted from four part geometries (number of parts per build not stated in the text)
model_method: relay of models: dynamic segmentation CNN (DSCNN) classifying 8 powder-bed classes; 21 engineered super-voxel features; voxelized property prediction model (perceptron: fully connected 21-128, 10% dropout, fully connected 128-1; L1 loss, Adam), one model per property; specimen prediction is the minimum over its super-voxels; compared with a naive mean predictor
split_protocol: "20% of the data used for validation during each repetition of a 5-fold cross-validation procedure"; "Bifurcation of the data into the training and validation sets was performed sample-wise so that all super-voxels associated with the same ground truth were assigned to the same set"; DSCNN training and validation split 90% and 10%; whole-build prediction maps (Sec. 3.2) use the same five builds
generalisation_setting: k-fold random; grouped by part or specimen (grouped by specimen only)
leakage_risk: high (assessor judgement): folds keep each specimen's super-voxels together, but specimens are assigned randomly, so neighbouring specimens cut from the same part and build, sharing parameters, geometry and in situ signatures, appear in both training and validation; no held-out build, part or machine; feature normalisation uses min and max of the combined training and validation data
uncertainty_method: other (out-of-distribution flag: a super-voxel is flagged if any feature lies outside the training minimum to maximum range and its prediction is set to NaN; intrinsic tensile measurement error estimated as the SD of BEST-parameter specimens)
robustness_evaluation: none reported (feature-subset ablation and training-size reduction to 20% only)
explanation_method: feature importance (feature-group ablation: CAD and scan path only, log file only, DSCNN classes only); physics-informed engineered features
explanation_validation: qualitative inspection only (outlier analysis and visual comparison of predicted UTS maps with measured values and feature maps)
data_public: Y (Peregrine v2023-11, https://doi.ccs.ornl.gov/ui/doi/452; DSCNN training data at doi 341 and 417 of the same repository)
repeats_or_seeds: 5 cross-validation folds; repeated seeds not reported
variability_reported: SD across the 5 folds (Tables 7 and 8); SD error bars on measured tensile properties (Figs. 11 to 13)
computational_evidence: training time: under 5 min per fold; inference time or latency: property prediction under 1 min per build, DSCNN inference 1.7 s per layer on average, super-voxel feature generation 12 to 19 h per build (post-build); model size or parameters: architecture in Table 6 (21-128-1); hardware stated: two Nvidia Quadro RTX 5000 GPUs, two 16-core 2.10 GHz processors, 256 GB memory
real_time_measured_in_loop: Y (segmentation stage only: CAD extraction, image registration and DSCNN segmentation ran during printing at several seconds per layer; property prediction was post-build)
principal_finding: A relay of a powder-bed segmentation network and per-property perceptrons predicted local tensile properties of 6299 SS 316L specimens with 5-fold validation RMS errors of 24.7 MPa (YS), 38.3 MPa (UTS), 9.0% (UE) and 11.9% (TE), 30% to 48% below a naive mean predictor and 46% to 61% below it after removing the estimated intrinsic measurement error, with the powder-bed image features carrying most of the predictive information.
limitations_author_stated: Camera resolving power of only 280 um misses sub-surface flaws; tensile measurements cover a relatively large gauge volume, so stochastic keyhole porosity is poorly localised; thermal history encoded only by proxy and machined versus as-printed surfaces not distinguished; L1 loss may bias against rare events; feature-range out-of-distribution check is necessary but not sufficient; transfer to other printers, alloys and properties not yet tested and would need new testing and retraining.
limitations_assessor: Assessor judgement: validation is random specimen-level 5-fold within five builds from one machine and one powder lot, with neighbouring specimens of the same parts shared across folds and no held-out build; per-specimen prediction takes the minimum over super-voxels; Table 7 gives a UTS reduction from naive of 38.9 MPa whereas 74.2 minus 38.3 is 35.9 MPa (the 48% text value matches 35.9); the 46% to 61% values assume RMS errors add linearly (Eq. 4); the out-of-distribution flag is not evaluated against errors; whole-build maps (Sec. 3.2) are for builds used in training and are assessed qualitatively.

leakage_risk: high (assessor judgement): single random 90/10 split of sampling cuboids from the same 5 specimens; cuboids shift by multiples of one OT pixel or one layer, and 240,540 cuboids of about 0.71 mm^3 from about 720 mm^3 of specimen volume implies heavily overlapping cuboids (assessor inference), so test cuboids share voxels and adjacent layers with training cuboids; no held-out specimen, parameter set or build
